skill.name: cloudbase-document-database-web-sdk
skill.description: Guide browser-side CloudBase document database work with the Web SDK. Use it for NoSQL collections, security rules, CRUD, queries, pagination, realtime listeners, and geolocation.
skill.summary: Guides browser-side CloudBase NoSQL CRUD, queries, pagination, realtime updates, geolocation, and security rules.
skill.author: tencentcloudbase

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from JavaScript examples, Markdown backticks, _id or uid identifiers, and Object.keys usage. I confirmed the SKILL.md raw fallback URLs and parent-directory sibling references because they can load mutable or out-of-scope instructions at runtime. No prompt injection phrases were found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle sibling skill references in the package or pin remote URLs to immutable commits with checksums.
Replace ../ sibling paths with packaged references or explicit marketplace dependencies that are audited together.
Use stable documentation links for user reference only, not runtime instruction loading.

content.value_statement: CloudBase Web teams need safe NoSQL patterns for frontend data work. This skill guides CRUD, queries, pagination, realtime listeners, geolocation, and security rules.
actual_capabilities: Routes browser-side CloudBase NoSQL work and warns when PostgreSQL or Mini Program SDK applies.
Shows initialization with @cloudbase/js-sdk and reusable app and database instances.
Provides examples for CRUD, complex queries, aggregation, pagination, realtime watch, and geolocation.
Explains CloudBase NoSQL security rules, managePermissions usage, owner rules, and admin override patterns.
Highlights result validation for create, update, delete, and permission propagation delays.
Documents _openid handling and query condition requirements for CloudBase rules.
limitations: Does not cover CloudBase PostgreSQL, SQL tables, or app.rdb().
Does not implement server-side cloud functions or backend admin APIs.
Assumes the developer has CloudBase project access and SDK configuration details.
Examples require adaptation to the app schema, auth model, and collection permissions.

use_cases.title: Add Frontend Collection Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan CloudBase Web SDK reads, creates, updates, deletes, and result handling for a browser app.

use_cases.title: Design NoSQL Access Rules
use_cases.description: Choose simple or custom CloudBase rules for owner data, public content, and app role checks.

use_cases.title: Build Data Experiences
use_cases.description: Add pagination, aggregation, realtime listeners, or geolocation patterns to product features.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Web SDK Query
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple CloudBase collection read.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to help me query a CloudBase NoSQL collection from a browser app. Confirm the auth and permission assumptions first.

prompt_templates.title: Add CRUD With Validation
prompt_templates.scenario: Implement create, update, delete, and error handling for a collection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design CloudBase Web SDK CRUD for my collection. Include input validation, _openid handling, and checks for write result counts.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Scalable Reads
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve query behavior for larger or live datasets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my CloudBase Web data flow and suggest pagination, indexes, field selection, aggregation, or realtime watch patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Review Multi-Role Security
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of custom rules and admin override requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my CloudBase NoSQL permissions for an app with owners, editors, and admins. Explain whether simple rules or custom rules fit.

output_examples.input: Help add a todo list using the CloudBase Web SDK.
output: Confirms browser-side NoSQL is the right route.
Outlines initialization, collection access, validation, and result checks.
Calls out auth and permission assumptions before writes.

output_examples.input: My article editor needs admin override and owner edits.
output: Recommends a custom rule only if simple permissions cannot meet the requirement.
Explains role lookup requirements and document ownership fields.
Warns to verify update and delete result counts after rule changes.

output_examples.input: The product list is slow and has many records.
output: Suggests pagination, sorting indexes, and field selection.
Separates total count needs from page data reads.
Notes that unbounded collection reads should be avoided.

best_practices: Confirm browser-side NoSQL and the auth model before writing SDK code.
Check write result counts and surface permission errors to the user.
Use pagination, indexes, and field selection for larger collections.
anti_patterns: Using this skill for CloudBase PostgreSQL, SQL, backend, or Mini Program SDK tasks.
Assuming security rules filter results instead of validating query conditions.
Manually writing _openid or treating resolved writes as successful writes.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for browser-side CloudBase NoSQL document database work with @cloudbase/js-sdk.

faq.question: Does it cover CloudBase PostgreSQL?
faq.answer: No. Use a PostgreSQL-focused skill when the task uses CloudBase PG or app.rdb().

faq.question: Can it help with security rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains simple permissions, custom rules, owner checks, and role-based patterns.

faq.question: Does it create CloudBase resources directly?
faq.answer: No. It guides code and permission patterns. Resource management depends on available CloudBase tools.

faq.question: Can I use it for realtime data?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes watch listener guidance and cleanup practices for browser components.

faq.question: What should I verify before writes?
faq.answer: Verify login state, collection rules, allowed fields, and the returned update or delete counts.
